subject: Prod load test caused cascading 5xx at peak - urgent escalation
messages:
From: Emily Porter <emily@greenlineanalytics.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: LaunchOps <launchops@greenlineanalytics.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Jul 2026 08:12:34 -0700
Subject: Load test -> large spike in 5xx and timeouts during scheduled ramp

Mina — we kicked off our production-scale load test at 07:50 PT this morning following the plan in the shared Drive folder. Around 07:58 we started seeing a sharp uptick in 5xx responses and end-user timeouts. By 08:05 error rate hit ~18% for the primary route and many of our clients started aggressive retries.

What we observed:
- Ramp target: 10x baseline traffic (steady 2k RPS to target 20k RPS over 6m)
- Symptoms: 502/504 and some 5xx variants, client timeouts at ~5s, and SDKs reporting socket errors
- Impact: partial degradation for customer-facing flows (search and chat)

Attached: loadtest-report-20260730.pdf, server-logs-07-30.zip.

Can you confirm whether this looks like a capacity shortfall vs. a cascading retry issue on our side? We need an immediate mitigation path — we can pause the test if you instruct us.

Thanks,
Emily Porter
Head of LaunchOps, Greenline Analytics
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Porter <emily@greenlineanalytics.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 30 Jul 2026 08:20:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Load test -> large spike in 5xx and timeouts during scheduled ramp

Emily — thanks for the quick heads up and the attachments. I’m escalating this to infra and the on-call team right now.

Immediate ask: please pause the test for 10 minutes while we validate a mitigation. We suspect a combination of overloaded serving queues plus an amplified retry pattern from your clients.

Initial mitigation options we can take quickly:
- Apply a short-lived rate cap at the edge for the affected route (10m)
- Temporarily route to a lower-capacity model variant with smaller memory footprint to reduce tail latency
- Enable a circuit-breaker to fail fast rather than allow slow requests to back up

We’ll also check for signs of KV cache churn and long tail GC on the serving nodes. I’ve looped in Karthik and the on-call infra.

Standby for an update in ~8–12 minutes.

— Mina
Mina Haddad
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, sean_gallagher@redwood.ai, david_kim@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 30 Jul 2026 08:24:51 -0700
Subject: Re: Load test -> large spike in 5xx and timeouts during scheduled ramp

On Thu, Jul 30, 2026 at 08:20 AM Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Emily — thanks for the quick heads up and the attachments. I’m escalating this to infra and the on-call team right now.

We’re seeing a pattern consistent with request fanout + KV cache invalidation at ~07:57 — a large fraction of requests missed local caches, producing a burst of backend fetches and elevated p99 latencies. In parallel we observed many client retries with minimal backoff which caused request amplification.

Actions taken (08:22–08:30 PT):
- Enabled a short edge rate-limit rule for the route (50% of target)
- Added a temporary routing rule to fall back to the smaller \"gpt-lite-v2\" variant for non-critical endpoints (search read-only paths)
- Throttled persistent heavy clients at the gateway level via token-based caps

Further notes:
- Recommend Greenline pause the load test and disable aggressive client-side retries (their SDK retry config indicates limited backoff).
- We will collect serving-side traces; attaching the retry-matrix.txt (excerpt) to the incident.

If Greenline pauses for 10m we can validate stability and then offer a controlled ramp with step-down guidance.

— Karthik (Infra on-call)
From: LaunchOps <launchops@greenlineanalytics.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 30 Jul 2026 08:33:10 -0700
Subject: Re: Load test -> large spike in 5xx and timeouts during scheduled ramp

On Thu, Jul 30, 2026 at 08:24 AM Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Actions taken (08:22–08:30 PT):
> - Enabled a short edge rate-limit rule for the route (50% of target)

Mina / Karthik — we have paused the test at 08:30 PT and will disable client retries now. We confirmed our test harness was configured with aggressive immediate retries (no exponential backoff) which explains the amplification.

We’ll hold for 10 minutes and restart only after your green. We’ll also send over our adjusted ramp script. Thanks for the quick triage.

— LaunchOps (Greenline)
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, sean_gallagher@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, david_kim@redwood.ai
Cc: Emily Porter <emily@greenlineanalytics.com>, LaunchOps <launchops@greenlineanalytics.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Jul 2026 08:48:05 -0700
Subject: Executive summary: Greenline load test -> spike in 5xx and retry amplification (timeline & next steps)

Team — quick exec summary for visibility. I’m keeping this concise in case Marissa / Sean want to loop in Sales / CS.

What happened:
- 07:50 PT: Greenline began schedule to ramp to 10x production traffic
- 07:57–08:05 PT: p50/p95 stable, p99 and p999 latency jumped; 5xx rate rose to ~18%
- Contributing factors: KV cache misses causing backend load + client-side aggressive retries without exponential backoff -> request amplification

Mitigation applied:
- Immediate: edge rate limit (short window), route non-critical paths to gpt-lite-v2, token-level caps for noisy clients
- Customer action: paused test and disabled retries for 10m while we validated

Impact and next steps:
- Customer-facing degraded for ~12 minutes; no data exfiltration; logs are attached for postmortem
- Next: coordinated re-run with staged step-ups, recommended client-side retry policy, and longer warmups to prime caches
- Action item: Offer Greenline an incident credit for disruption and a joint runbook session. Marissa, can you engage CS/AM on credits + a follow-up QBR?

I’ve opened PD-998234 and uploaded artifacts to the shared Drive. We should schedule a 30m postmortem with Greenline tomorrow to go over runbook and SDK defaults.

— Mina
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: Emily Porter <emily@greenlineanalytics.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: LaunchOps <launchops@greenlineanalytics.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 31 Jul 2026 15:24:01 -0700
Subject: Re: Executive summary: Greenline load test -> spike in 5xx and retry amplification (timeline & next steps)

Thanks Mina — appreciate the fast triage and the mitigation steps. We reviewed the logs and confirmed that once SDK retries were disabled the error rate dropped to baseline. We’re good to resume a controlled ramp tomorrow at 09:00 PT following your step-up guidance.

One quick ask for the postmortem: can Redwood include recommendations for SDK retry defaults and a short checklist we can share with our engineers (backoff windows, jitter, and warmup guidance)?

Emily
Head of LaunchOps, Greenline Analytics
